mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE > 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.05) between INDPRO 4-month decline and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in the RSAFS (personal savings) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates households are drawing down savings to finance spending despite higher rates, signaling resilient demand and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls > -5% in the same month
regime_hint: monetary tightening with resilient household demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls > -5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both GDPC1 and HOUST above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening housing and overall demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 and HOUST above 12-month MA and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of PAYEMS above 12-month MA for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a broad-based supply expansion, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO above 12-month MA for 5 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when INDPRO is above 12-month MA for five months and CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%.
